quarterly_data.signal: 10-K fiscal 2026 revenue by business unit: CMBU $43,085 million (32% of total), CDBU $37,592 million (28%), MCBU $36,601 million (27%) and AEBU $15,886 million (12%), versus $13,524 million, $7,229 million, $11,859 million and $4,753 million in fiscal 2025; business-unit operating income was $31,225 million (CMBU), $29,539 million (CDBU), $29,208 million (MCBU) and $11,217 million (AEBU).

10-K strategic customer agreements: in fiscal 2026 Micron executed take-or-pay strategic customer agreements with a number of customers, with binding commitments for specific volumes over multi-year terms and, for the majority, pricing subject to minimum and maximum bands; Micron expects these agreements, even at floor pricing levels, to yield gross margins meaningfully above its peak quarterly margins in any past cycle. It received $12.75 billion of customer cash deposits in 2026, nearly all scheduled to be repaid between 2029 and 2031, and letters of credit issued or committed totaled $7 billion as of September 3, 2026. Remaining performance obligations were approximately $134 billion at September 3, 2026 (not material a year earlier), of which $13 billion was recognized as contract liabilities; approximately one-fourth is expected to be recognized as revenue over the next twelve months and all within five years. Micron says the deposits are intended to secure future production capacity and supply availability.
quarterly_data.figure: RPO ~$134 billion (September 3, 2026); customer deposits $12.75 billion; letters of credit $7 billion; ~one-fourth within 12 months

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K capex and capacity: purchase obligations for the acquisition of property, plant and equipment were approximately $4.18 billion as of September 3, 2026, substantially all expected to be paid within one year; government incentives related to capital expenditures had reduced property, plant and equipment by $10.93 billion, of which $6.43 billion pertained to 2026 expenditures. Micron states it generally utilizes all of its existing manufacturing capacity.
quarterly_data.figure: PP&E purchase obligations ~$4.18 billion; incentives reduced PP&E by $10.93 billion ($6.43 billion for 2026)

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K supply constraints: Micron states that shortages or increases in lead times are currently occurring with respect to some materials and components (such as chemicals, silicon wafers, gases, photoresists, semiconductors and substrates), that constraints for certain materials and integrated circuit components could limit its bit shipments, and that its ability to sell certain products has been impeded when components necessary for the finished products were not available from third parties; increasing AI-driven demand may intensify competition for critical materials, manufacturing equipment and advanced packaging capacity.
